newsitem.title: USA: Odwalla reports loss after juice recall.
newsitem.headline: Odwalla reports loss after juice recall.

text.p: Odwalla Inc. Tuesday reported a $4.8 million first quarter loss, reflecting costs associated with the company's recall of some of its juice products after a bacterial outbreak.
Odwalla became linked to an outbreak of E.coli in October in which 50 people were sickened with the bacteria, many of them after drinking Odwalla apple juice.
One child died from complications said to result from drinking Odwalla juice.

The juice-maker, which built a business on producing wholesome natural juices, recalled 16 of its products immediately after the first E. coli cases were reported, removing them from 4,600 stores in its distribution region.
For the three months ended in November, Odwalla said it lost $4.8 million or 98 cents a share, compared with a loss of $120,000, or 2 cents a share, a year ago.
Sales rose to $14.1 million from $12.4 million. Operating expenses were $12.9 million vs. $5.9 million a year ago.
Odwalla said it experienced a significant reduction in sales of all products after the recall of products containing apple juice and the expanded recall of its carrot and vegetable products.
Odwalla also incurred significant costs for the product recalled and destroyed, legal and marketing expenses.

Additional costs were incurred with the introduction of the flash pasteurization process. Direct recall costs totalled $3.8 million in the first quarter, including $700,000 of estimated direct costs for the rest of the year.
